# Independent numerical ODE prerequisite pairs — intake proposal

Draft proposal only. No ML consumer is a prerequisite. All procedures and proofs remain to be authored.

### P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error

**Pages:** one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error / one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error-examples. **Scope:** Define a one-step method $\Psi_h(t,y)$, local defect $\|\Psi_h(t,y(t))-y(t+h)\|$, and stability. For a fixed interval $[0,T]$ and exact solutions staying in a compact tube, state the order-$p$ hypothesis as a uniform local defect $\le Ch^{p+1}$ and the one-step stability bound $\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|$. Derive these premises for Euler when $f$ is $C^1$ in time and state with bounded derivatives on that tube; any named Runge–Kutta method must state its order conditions and required derivatives separately. **Proof route:** Taylor-expand the exact flow and the selected method increment, bound remainders uniformly on the tube, and prove the stated stability estimate; do not infer an order from the method label alone. **Examples:** Euler on a scalar linear field; a nonsmooth field where its local order drops. **Requires:** thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution, thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives, and a proved Taylor remainder estimate; the local error calculation is explicit, but a numerical-analysis source remains unaudited. **Sources:** Chen et al., neural-ODE Appendix B/C and numerical issues, PDF pp. 13–16, and Papamakarios et al., continuous-flow section pp. 31–33, discuss solver use but do not prove the error theorem. Acquire/read a matching numerical-ODE source before publication. This pair precedes P-NUM-ODE-02.

### P-NUM-ODE-02 — Global ODE and log-density integration error

**Pages:** global-ode-and-density-error / global-ode-and-density-error-examples. **Scope:** Under P-NUM-ODE-01’s uniform order-$p$ defect/stability bounds and a fixed finite interval, derive $\max_n\|y_n-y(t_n)\|\le C_T h^p$ by the discrete Grönwall recurrence. For a continuous normalizing flow augment the state by $\ell'=-\operatorname{div}f(x,t)$ and bound the log-density error separately. For Euler, $f\in C^2$ with bounded derivatives on a compact tube makes the augmented vector field locally Lipschitz and supports a local $O(h^2)$ defect; for order $p>1$, require the method-specific order conditions and enough bounded derivatives of the augmented field, or state a separate quadrature theorem with matching smoothness. $C^2$ regularity alone does not justify arbitrary order-$p$ convergence. State solver, quadrature, and state-error contributions separately. A state trajectory error alone does not control log-density or adjoint-gradient error. **Proof route:** derive $e_{n+1}\le(1+Lh)e_n+Ch^{p+1}$, iterate it, then apply a second bound to the augmented/log-density component under its own local defect and stability estimates. **Examples:** Euler global error for a linear flow; same state solver with a separately refined density quadrature. **Requires:** P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error; discrete Grönwall and the divergence-Lipschitz estimate, proved locally if no exact supplier exists. **Sources:** Chen et al. pp. 13–16 and Papamakarios et al. pp. 31–33 discuss solver use and numerical issues but do not prove these error theorems; the local defect/stability/Grönwall proof remains a clearly specified authoring obligation. ML-58 — Neural ODEs and continuous normalizing flows and ML-61 — Conditional flow matching and transport paths consume this only when numerical error is claimed.


## Binding consumed contract

**P-NUM-ODE-01/02.** Fix d≥1, T>0, h=T/N, N≥1, a common open time-state domain and a compact solution tube with positive margin. Use Euclidean vector norms and induced operator norms. The exact IVP solution y and every numerical stage/state in the theorem stay in that tube. A one-step map Ψ_h(t,·) is defined there and satisfies, for constants C,L≥0 independent of N and j, ||Ψ_h(t_j,y(t_j))−y(t_(j+1))||≤C h^(p+1) and ||Ψ_h(t_j,v)−Ψ_h(t_j,w)||≤(1+Lh)||v−w||. With initial error e₀≤C₀h^p, prove max_j e_j≤(C₀e^(LT)+C(e^(LT)−1)/L)h^p for L>0, and (C₀+CT)h^p for L=0. Derive Euler's C and L from f∈C¹ with finite field, time-derivative and state-Jacobian bounds on the tube; derive each higher-order tableau's defect separately from its exact derivative/order conditions. For augmented log density ℓ′=−div f, Euler requires f∈C² with bounded relevant derivatives of f and div f, the augmented tube, and a separate state/log-defect estimate; no arbitrary higher order follows from C². Local proof route: Taylor/integral remainder, invariant-tube admissibility and geometric-sum recurrence, using actual root ODE/Taylor/Grönwall suppliers. Matching source design: Hairer–Wanner Ch. III §§III.2–III.5, PDF pp. 4–11/printed 60–67, as recorded by the recovery packet. NA-15 supplies concrete conditions to instantiate the abstract theorem, never a prerequisite of the generic theorem. Consumers: NA-15, NA-18 notation only, NA-21 when numerical shooting is quantified, NA-45 matching ODE terms.


The abstract recurrence/global-error theorem is owned by P-NUM-ODE-02; P-NUM-ODE-01 owns local defect/stability definitions and Euler derivation. NA-15 owns concrete higher-order tableaux. The recurrence accepts hypotheses directly and must never depend back on NA-15.

## XA-01 — extend canonical rare-event/SMC guarantees; do not duplicate algorithms

**Existing home:** `library/bayesian-computational-statistics/feynman-kac-particle-filters.md` and its examples. Existing `alg-sequential-importance-resampling`, `alg-multinomial-and-residual-offspring-resampling`, `thm-sequential-particle-estimator-is-unbiased`, `lem-feynman-kac-path-measures-satisfy-forward-recursion` retain their homes. Existing IS unbiasedness, finite variance and CLT are already covered; no new IS pair.

**New delta.** Integration owner: optimization/statistics RARE1 absorbs this amendment; no separate pair or competing procedure. Define a finite sequence of nested events/levels with exact stopped transition kernels and potentials 0≤G≤1. Prove measurability of finite-budget stopped kernels (or a declared exact-hitting oracle), connection of their Feynman–Kac normalizer to the target event probability, and error of any time-discretized crossing approximation separately. Use existing SMC product-normalizer estimator; its unbiasedness is reused only under all positive-prefix-normalizer/full-resampling hypotheses. Then prove a finite-horizon L2 bound with explicit dependence on number of levels, prefix probabilities, bounded normalized potentials and kernel mixing. A safe first contract is an O(1/N) **absolute** mean-square bound for a fixed number of bounded-potential levels, proved by conditional variance and induction. Relative error divides by the squared rare probability and may be huge. An efficiency claim uniform in rarity needs an additional theorem and actual lower bounds/minorization; not “splitting reduces variance” by name.

**Missing local suppliers / owner.** Local to this amendment: stopped-kernel construction and cemetery handling; Feynman–Kac event identity; conditional empirical variance identity for the actual resampling procedure; finite-level martingale/variance recursion; bias from approximate crossing/hitting kernels. Existing finite-horizon SMC unbiasedness does not by itself imply finite-particle accuracy or uniform-in-time stability (the canonical page explicitly says so). No adaptive-level unbiasedness without its separate order-statistic/martingale proof. Root must assign this amendment to the statistics guarantee owner and check affected consumers if an existing statement changes; prefer new theorem carriers without altering original definitions.

**Examples.** Reliability chain crossing; extinction estimate; all particles die (zero estimate, not algorithmic proof of zero probability); an IS proposal with infinite weighted second moment; same budget splitting with worse relative error. **Sources:** Cérou–Del Moral–Furon–Guyader, “Sequential Monte Carlo for rare event estimation,” Statistics and Computing 22 (2012), pp. 795–808, DOI `10.1007/s11222-011-9231-6`; Del Moral, *Feynman–Kac Formulae* (2004), particle variance/martingale chapters, DOI `10.1007/978-1-4684-9393-1`. Exact source hypotheses are intake obligations.

pairs.methods_and_promises: **A scope.** Finite-state CTMC with reactions nu_j and nonnegative state propensities a_j, bounded total hazard; holding survival exp(-a0(x)t), reaction selection a_j/a0, absorbing a0=0. Exact Gillespie direct method and next-reaction clock representation; prove resulting law/generator equals the declared CTMC, not the chemical physical system. Extend to finite reaction networks on countable states only under an explicitly proved nonexplosion Lyapunov criterion. Construct Poisson random-time-change X=X0+sum nu_j Y_j(integral a_j(X)ds), and shared/minimum-intensity coupling with exact marginals for comparison/MLMC. Time-varying hazard uses integrated hazard inversion with a certified solve or dominating thinning with a proved envelope. **Proof/prereqs:** own exponential race, temporal Poisson independent increments, strong Markov/memoryless recursion or direct finite-path density construction, nonexplosion and jump martingale/isometry if later consumed. Existing spatial Poisson count theorem alone does not supply this. **B:** birth-death, absorbing extinction, explosive pure birth with rates n², invalid hazard upper bound. **Deps:** published Poisson/exponential laws; biology agent owns master equation/uniformization/FSP and consumes these exact simulation interfaces. **Cost:** O(R) direct event selection or verified O(log R) update tree, event count expectation required; zero hazard handled. **Sources:** Gillespie, J Comput Phys 22 (1976), exact stochastic simulation; Anderson/Kurtz, Stochastic Analysis of Biochemical Systems, random-time-change/coupling chapters. Reads pending.

pairs.methods_and_promises:
**Disposition:** extend-existing substantial algorithm/error guarantee. `ex-quantile-coupling-on-the-real-line` already proves generalized inverse Q(U) has the target law; `lem-randomized-probability-integral-transform` treats the reverse randomized CDF transform. Do not redefine those statistical transformations as a new method. The example is contextual rather than a legal logical supplier; consume `thm-probability-law-and-distribution-function-correspondence` and promote only the needed generalized-inverse sublevel identity to a typed prerequisite with proof/source attribution, avoiding a duplicate broad quantile-coupling theorem. The new guarantee is actual bit/stream implementation and finite-distribution error plus Box-Muller sampling, absent from inspected canonical methods.

**Randomness model:** independent ideal fair bits B_j on an explicitly constructed countable product probability space; U=sum B_j 2^-j has uniform law by dyadic cylinder intervals and continuity of measure. Disjoint bit blocks/streams preserve independence. A b-bit K uniform on {0,...,2^b-1} gives U_b=(K+1/2)2^-b, coupling |U-U_b|<=2^(-b-1), hence W1 at most that and Kolmogorov discrepancy at most 2^-b. Finite-support versus continuous law has total variation distance1, so no TV-small assertion. Independence of finite outputs requires disjoint independent bit blocks; recycling bits changes dependence.

**Practical finite generators:** define an actual full-period LCG modulo 2^w with odd increment and multiplier a congruent1 mod4, w>=2; prove full period by induction modulo powers of2 using affine iterate arithmetic, and state finite state/period bound for every deterministic generator. With random uniform initial state each single state is uniform, but adjacent states satisfy the recurrence and are not independent. Give a counter-based stream interface as a deterministic keyed permutation of finite counters; a random permutation/key model or computational pseudorandomness assumption must be explicit, never an IID theorem. No cryptographic-quality claim or empirical-test proof of independence. Non-overlapping blocks avoid exact reuse only within certified period; do not imply probabilistic independence.

**Variates:** inverse CDF already canonical; add implemented bracketed inverse with certified |F(xhat)-u|<=epsilon on a monotone continuous CDF, finite-bit U discrepancy adds to Kolmogorov error (plus any actual CDF approximation error). Spatial error requires density f>=m>0 on the inversion bracket, and tails handled separately. Discrete CDF binary search gives exact categorical law under ideal U, finite-bit count discrepancy bounded per threshold; Bernoulli rational sampling via unbiased integer rejection has geometric expected bit/block cost and budget failure; finite budget discarded separately.

Box-Muller uses independent ideal U1,U2 in (0,1), Z1=sqrt(-2 log U1)cos(2pi U2), Z2=sqrt(-2 log U1)sin(2pi U2). Prove independent standard-normal density by polar change of variables and product density normalization; same-pair polar Jacobian/measure change prerequisite must be proved if not published. Finite bits imply bounded normal tails and discrete output, never exact Gaussian; couple midpoint U_b to U, restrict U1>=delta and guard angular/endpoint arithmetic, derivative bounds give explicit Wasserstein/bounded-Lipschitz output error on that event, while discarded event probability <=delta+2^-b. Tail expectations use proved Gaussian/Rayleigh moments and Cauchy-Schwarz; elementary log/sqrt/trig evaluation errors supplied by precision owner add through those derivative bounds. No Ziggurat implementation required if not fully specified/proved; rejection algorithm may be a later optional genuinely new optimization only with envelope/area proof. Gaussian samples in SDE algorithms are ideal-law or approximate-law with this additional coupling error propagated; no invisible exact-normal finite-bit oracle.

**Same-frontier prerequisites:** product independent-bit construction (reuse existing countable product theorem if available, otherwise own cylinder extension), dyadic uniform law, LCG modular induction, stopping/rejection cost, finite-CDF inverse residual, polar transform identity, truncated-transform coupling and arithmetic error propagation. Root must map any newly located canonical supplier instead of creating duplicate items. **Examples:** low-bit LCG correlation/lattice, normal tail truncation, zero endpoint log failure, inverse CDF near vanishing density. **Cost:** random bits, rejection count, integer arithmetic, precision and transform calls; bit cost distinct from real-RAM sampling oracle cost. **Sources, unread candidates:** Devroye, Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation, author's full-book portal https://luc.devroye.org/rnbookindex.html ; L'Ecuyer RNG publications https://www.iro.umontreal.ca/~lecuyer/myftp/papers.html ; Box/Muller, Ann Math Stat 29 (1958), https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177706645 . Canonical quantile source https://sites.math.duke.edu/~rtd/PTE/PTE5_011119.pdf .

### NA-45 — Error budgets for computational inference

**Pages:** error-budgets-for-computational-inference / error-budgets-for-computational-inference-examples.

**Scope:** Define a target-to-computation path for an integral, likelihood, or SDE expectation and prove a pathwise triangle-inequality decomposition into deterministic quadrature/discretization, algebraic solve/optimization residual, finite-precision, Monte Carlo/randomization, approximation, data-sampling, and model error where each term is defined. State that some terms may be random and need their own mode (pathwise, in expectation, or probability). Root-sum-square requires covariance/independence premises. A solver rate that vanishes under refinement does not remove a fixed model/score bias. This page supplies numerical bookkeeping, not posterior calibration or inferential coverage.

**Proof route:** Insert intermediate exact targets and apply the triangle inequality along the computation path. For randomized terms, derive a variance sum only after proving centering and cross-covariance conditions; keep deterministic truncation/conditioning terms separate. Reuse P-NUM-ODE/SDE only for their exact solver contracts and do not infer model correctness.

**Examples:** quadrature plus optimizer residual in a likelihood normalizer; MC standard error shrinking while SDE time-discretization bias remains; numerical refinement with a nonzero learned-model bias.

**Requires:** NA-01, NA-12, NA-13, NA-14, NA-39, NA-40, NA-41, NA-42, NA-43, and NA-44; independent planned P-NUM-ODE-01/02 and P-NUM-SDE-01/02 only for the matching solver terms.

**Sources:** Owen, Simple Monte Carlo Ch. 2 §§2.1–2.3 and 2.9, printed pp. 15–21 and 35–36 / PDF pp. 16–22 and 36–37, selected sections read: https://artowen.su.domains/mc/Ch-intro.pdf; Practical QMC Chs. 15 and 17, complete main text/notes/exercises read at PDF pp. 11–72 and 103–160: https://artowen.su.domains/mc/practicalqmc.pdf; Giles, full §3 Theorem 3.1 and proof, PDF pp. 1–11: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/gilesm/files/OPRE_2008.pdf; Higham–Mao–Stuart, journal pp. 1041–1056 / PDF pp. 1–16 read, later pp. 1057–1063 unread: https://authors.library.caltech.edu/records/1wrtf-vyz04/files/s0036142901389530.pdf; Boyd–Vandenberghe §§9.2, 9.3.1 and 9.5.1–9.5.3 read at physical PDF pp. 477–483 and 498–506: https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/bv_cvxbook.pdf; Hansen, Ch. 4 all 29 slides, Ch. 5 all 27 slides, and Ch. 3 pp. 1–6 read: https://www2.imm.dtu.dk/~pcha/DIP/. # Independent numerical ODE prerequisite pairs — intake proposal

Draft proposal only. No ML consumer is a prerequisite. All procedures and proofs remain to be authored.

### P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error

**Pages:** one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error / one-step-ode-consistency-and-local-error-examples. **Scope:** Define a one-step method $\Psi_h(t,y)$, local defect $\|\Psi_h(t,y(t))-y(t+h)\|$, and stability. For a fixed interval $[0,T]$ and exact solutions staying in a compact tube, state the order-$p$ hypothesis as a uniform local defect $\le Ch^{p+1}$ and the one-step stability bound $\|\Psi_h(t,u)-\Psi_h(t,v)\|\le(1+Lh)\|u-v\|$. Derive these premises for Euler when $f$ is $C^1$ in time and state with bounded derivatives on that tube; any named Runge–Kutta method must state its order conditions and required derivatives separately. **Proof route:** Taylor-expand the exact flow and the selected method increment, bound remainders uniformly on the tube, and prove the stated stability estimate; do not infer an order from the method label alone. **Examples:** Euler on a scalar linear field; a nonsmooth field where its local order drops. **Requires:** thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-a-maximal-ode-solution, thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives, and a proved Taylor remainder estimate; the local error calculation is explicit, but a numerical-analysis source remains unaudited. **Sources:** Chen et al., neural-ODE Appendix B/C and numerical issues, PDF pp. 13–16, and Papamakarios et al., continuous-flow section pp. 31–33, discuss solver use but do not prove the error theorem. Acquire/read a matching numerical-ODE source before publication. This pair precedes P-NUM-ODE-02.

### P-NUM-ODE-02 — Global ODE and log-density integration error

**Pages:** global-ode-and-density-error / global-ode-and-density-error-examples. **Scope:** Under P-NUM-ODE-01’s uniform order-$p$ defect/stability bounds and a fixed finite interval, derive $\max_n\|y_n-y(t_n)\|\le C_T h^p$ by the discrete Grönwall recurrence. For a continuous normalizing flow augment the state by $\ell'=-\operatorname{div}f(x,t)$ and bound the log-density error separately. For Euler, $f\in C^2$ with bounded derivatives on a compact tube makes the augmented vector field locally Lipschitz and supports a local $O(h^2)$ defect; for order $p>1$, require the method-specific order conditions and enough bounded derivatives of the augmented field, or state a separate quadrature theorem with matching smoothness. $C^2$ regularity alone does not justify arbitrary order-$p$ convergence. State solver, quadrature, and state-error contributions separately. A state trajectory error alone does not control log-density or adjoint-gradient error. **Proof route:** derive $e_{n+1}\le(1+Lh)e_n+Ch^{p+1}$, iterate it, then apply a second bound to the augmented/log-density component under its own local defect and stability estimates. **Examples:** Euler global error for a linear flow; same state solver with a separately refined density quadrature. **Requires:** P-NUM-ODE-01 — One-step ODE consistency and local error; discrete Grönwall and the divergence-Lipschitz estimate, proved locally if no exact supplier exists. **Sources:** Chen et al. pp. 13–16 and Papamakarios et al. pp. 31–33 discuss solver use and numerical issues but do not prove these error theorems; the local defect/stability/Grönwall proof remains a clearly specified authoring obligation. ML-58 — Neural ODEs and continuous normalizing flows and ML-61 — Conditional flow matching and transport paths consume this only when numerical error is claimed.

## NA15 explicit extension — `TIME-SSP` owner and stabilized Chebyshev stepping

**Classification:** extend-existing, genuinely new time guarantees. Reuse canonical `def-chebyshev-polynomials-first-and-second-kind`, `thm-chebyshev-multiple-angle-identities`, `lem-chebyshev-degree-leading-coefficients-and-extreme-values`; do not reintroduce approximation polynomials.

**SSP method:** SSPRK(3,3): Y1=u+h f(u), Y2=3u/4+(Y1+h f(Y1))/4, unew=u/3+2(Y2+h f(Y2))/3. Prove third order by actual Taylor coefficients. If the forward Euler map preserves a specified convex invariant set C or satisfies a convex functional Phi(u+h f(u))<=Phi(u) for every u in C and 0<=h<=h_FE, convexity of C/Phi proves every stage and update preserve that property with coefficient1 and same timestep bound. State the premise at each stage and include boundary/time-dependent operators via augmented time or actual stage times. TVD is licensed only when the spatial forward-Euler theorem supplies Phi=TV and its CFL. No universal SSP claim for RK4. PDE PE04 consumes `TIME-SSP` = this NA15 proof interface. Missing lemma convex composition is owned NA15; no unowned key.

**Stabilized explicit method:** first order R_s(z)=T_s(1+z/s²), s>=1, implemented by y0=y, y1=y+(h/s²)Ay and yj=2 y_(j-1)-y_(j-2)+(2h/s²)A y_(j-1). For the second-order linear RKC variant s>=2, use w1=3/(s²-1), b=(s²-1)/(3s²), a=1-b and R_s(z)=a+b T_s(1+w1 z). Evaluate the same three-term Chebyshev recurrence with h/s² replaced by w1 h and output a y0+b ys. Prove T_s'(1)=s² and T_s''(1)=s²(s²-1)/3 by differentiating the recurrence; hence R(0)=R'(0)=R''(0)=1 and actual order2 on fixed linear autonomous systems. Stability intervals are [-2s²,0] for order1 and [-2(s²-1)/3,0] for order2 because |T_s(x)|<=1 on [-1,1] and 0<b<1. For self-adjoint nonpositive A in the declared inner product, spectral theorem gives contraction when h rho(-A) is within that interval. For nonsymmetric A eigenvalue inclusion alone is insufficient; require a proved functional calculus or bounded diagonalization constants. Inhomogeneous equations use an explicitly augmented system with forcing regularity or separate Duhamel discretization.

Use s~sqrt(h rho) stages and count s matrix-vector products, versus O(h rho) forward Euler substeps for the same macro h. This is a stability-work comparison, not an accuracy speedup theorem. Prove global fixed-T order from local Taylor remainder and stable propagation with explicit ||A³u|| bound; do not claim mesh-uniform order from bounded scalar R alone. Internal stage perturbations satisfy a forced Chebyshev recurrence; use U_j with |U_j(x)|<=j+1 to bound O(s² max perturbation) on the stable segment and include roundoff/action errors. Nonlinear RKC needs an actual nonlinear stage construction and order proof; this linear variant does not supply one silently. Examples: semidiscrete self-adjoint heat, stiff reaction negative spectrum, nonnormal failure, stage-roundoff growth. Source candidates (unread): https://www.unige.ch/~hairer/books.html ; https://doi.org/10.1137/S003614450036757X (SSP review locator, exact record to verify before binding); Sommeijer/Shampine/Verwer RKC algorithm via author portal https://homepages.cwi.nl/~verwer/ .

## NA15 nonlinear RKC construction (bind instead of stopping at linear example)

Preserve the simple linear proof above as the stability model, and include this actual autonomous nonlinear second-order stabilized explicit RK recurrence. For s>=2 set w1=3/(s²-1), b0=b1=b2=1/4 and b_j=(j²-1)/(3j²) for j>=2, a_j=1-b_j. Let Y0=y, Y1=y+b1 w1 h f(y). For j=2,...,s define mu_j=2 b_j/b_(j-1), nu_j=-b_j/b_(j-2), mt_j=2 b_j w1/b_(j-1), gt_j=-a_(j-1) mt_j, and

Yj=(1-mu_j-nu_j)y+mu_j Y_(j-1)+nu_j Y_(j-2)+mt_j h f(Y_(j-1))+gt_j h f(y).

Output Ys. It is an explicit RK method because every stage is an affine combination of y and earlier RHS evaluations. At constant f its stage abscissae follow c1=b1 w1 and c_j=b_j w1 j² for j>=2, hence c_s=1. Derive the coefficient of f'f by expanding the recurrence through h², or equivalently use the one order2 rooted tree plus actual scalar stability polynomial a_s+b_s T_s(1+w1 z), to prove final coefficient1/2. This equivalence is justified only through order2; higher-order linear matching does not establish nonlinear order. For f in C2 with bounded derivatives on a controlled tube and all stages admitted, Taylor remainder plus one-step Lipschitz propagation proves global order2 for fixed s on fixed T. The long real stability interval remains a scalar linear/normal-matrix guarantee; nonlinear dissipation, positivity, SSP and stiffness-uniform accuracy do not follow. Time-dependent f is handled by augmenting t'=1 and using the actual derived c_j, not an arbitrary stage-time guess. Include an explicit finite-stage domain check and s-dependent roundoff amplification. Damped w0>1 variants are optional only with separately verified coefficients; the undamped scheme already has the proved interval and actual nonlinear method.

* **NA-15/17/18:** distinguish absolute stability, positive invariance, conservation and certified adaptive global error. Crosslink XD-03 rather than imply stiff solvers protect nonnegative biological states. Event/history/stiffness extensions remain sibling ownership.
* **NA-22:** particle/symplectic examples must state domain/collision restrictions and actual time-integrator invariants. A Hamiltonian interpretation is a mathematical stipulated model. Neither discrete energy drift plots nor conserved semidiscrete momentum prove a continuum particle limit.
* **NA-23/24/25:** graph/renewal boundary rows are not ordinary rectangular Dirichlet rows. Diffusive L2 stability does not imply positivity; add actual maximum-principle conditions only when proved. Inflow renewal and junction routing go to XD-04/09.
* **NA-26/27:** retain scalar BV entropy scope; it cannot supply multi-species positivity or aggregation/fragmentation moment conservation. The new methods receive independent proofs.
* **NA-28–36:** interval-edge graph trace, renewal inflow trace and particle boundary correction are distinct from simplex H1 trace. Reuse exact established interfaces, supply missing geometry locally. No arbitrary SPH/RBF convergence via Céa unless a real coercive Galerkin structure is proved.
* **NA-39/42:** identify randomness and coupling: particle loading, jump paths, resampling and empirical initial measures differ. Do not transfer independent-level variance proofs to correlated levels or claim N^−1/2 uniform transport error from a scalar MC CLT.
* **NA-43/44/45:** require forward model/sensitivity discretization terms in parameter estimation/design. Identifiability of an exact statistical model does not certify a numerically thresholded Jacobian rank. Preserve approximation, sampling, solver, regularization and model error separately; finite projection/cutoff bias is explicit.

A: `ewald-periodic-potentials-and-particle-mesh-error`.

On a specified 3D torus, finitely many distinct positions x_i and real charges q_i with sum q_i=0 define the mean-zero periodic Poisson distribution -Delta u=4pi(sum q_i delta_xi). Specify the lattice shape, self subtraction, Gaussian parameter alpha, real/reciprocal cutoffs, output convention and arithmetic model. The naive Coulomb lattice sum is conditional; the periodic mean-zero definition controls the summation convention. Prove absolute convergence of the split sums, alpha independence, explicit Gaussian real-tail/reciprocal-tail bounds using lattice shell counts, and differentiated force bounds away from collisions. pairs.methods_and_promises:
**Exact scope.** Use column probability vectors: finite Q has Q_ij≥0 for i≠j, 1ᵀQ=0. For ν≥max_j(−Q_jj)>0, P=I+Q/ν is column stochastic and

`p(t)=exp(tQ)p0 = Σ_{k≥0} exp(−νt)(νt)^k/k! P^k p0`.

Define finite Poisson-series accumulation with a certified tail bound and a maximum term budget; ν=0 returns p0. Prove nonnegative substochastic partial sums, l1 omitted probability exactly the scalar Poisson tail for normalized p0, and l1 total transient error ≤tail + accumulated arithmetic/algebraic error. A floating-point subtraction `1−sum` is not automatically a certified tail; use controlled interval sums or a proved geometric/Chernoff tail bound. Large νt must use time splitting or stable Poisson recurrences rather than silently underflowing `exp(−νt)`.

Finite-state projection: for an increasing finite set F in a countable nonexplosive chain, kill the process on first exit, or append an absorbing cemetery state carrying escaped mass. The killed state probability is componentwise ≤the full marginal restricted to F. Under a common-process coupling, l1 error after embedding the killed vector in the full state space equals lost mass; the absorbing projection including the cemetery state instead gives an observable error bound for bounded observables, with oscillation factor stated. Returning trajectories are a reason killed and restricted full probabilities differ. Adaptive enlargement requires a finite budget and certificates from each actual projection; existence of a finite set meeting a tolerance is separate.
pairs.proof_route: **Proof route and local suppliers.** (1) `def-xd-finite-column-generator` and `lem-xd-uniformized-matrix-is-stochastic`; (2) finite matrix power series convergence/term differentiation and coefficient identity, reuse the general matrix-functions supplier if available; otherwise prove these finite-dimensional facts here before use; (3) Poisson law/tail recurrence and a controlled tail majorant; (4) uniformization identity by commuting Q=ν(P−I), uniqueness of finite linear ODE; (5) killed path coupling and first-exit decomposition, using time-agent CTMC construction/nonexplosion, or prove the finite stopped-path construction locally; (6) finite/countable projection monotonicity and loss certificate by summing nonnegative path probabilities; (7) telescoping perturbation error in substochastic l1 contractions. No unproved assertion of arbitrary countable-generator nonexplosion.
pairs.examples: **B examples.** Two-state gating; finite birth–death model with computed Poisson tail; countable immigration/death projected to F with loss monitor; equal mean but different distributions showing that a deterministic concentration ODE is not a master-equation solver.

**Disposition:** genuinely-new. No canonical Parareal/MGRIT carrier located by filename/content searches. **Methods:** for fine propagator F and coarse G over macro H, U0^k=u0, U_(n+1)^(k+1)=G(U_n^(k+1))+F(U_n^k)-G(U_n^k); initialize by serial G. Parallel F evaluations followed by serial coarse correction; finite sweep/time budgets. Target is the sequential fine trajectory, not the exact ODE unless F's error is added.

**Proof:** consistency induction proves U_n^k=F^n(u0) for n<=k, hence exact fine solution after at most N sweeps in exact arithmetic, independent of a contraction assertion. For useful convergence, assume on a common invariant tube ||G(x)-G(y)||<=a||x-y|| and ||(F-G)(x)-(F-G)(y)||<=b||x-y||, with a<=1+CH, b<=C H^(q+1). Error recurrence e_(n+1)^(k+1)<=a e_n^(k+1)+b e_n^k yields by induction binomial(n,k)b^k max(1,a)^n times a bounded initial-error envelope, with endpoint conventions and all iterates remaining in tube; fixed T then gives iteration-dependent acceleration. Initial and fine/coarse algebraic errors are additive forcing, not hidden exactness. For oscillatory/nonnormal or unstable coarse maps, a,b may make the bound useless.

**MGRIT:** define linear all-at-once bidiagonal time operator A_t for u_n-Phi u_(n-1)=r_n, F/C splitting, ideal interpolation/elimination Schur complement with exact coarse propagator Phi^m, practical coarse propagator Psi, F/FCF relaxation and coarse correction. Derive actual two-grid error matrix E=S_post(I-P A_c^-1 R A_t)S_pre in declared block norm, prove residual/error equivalence and convergence when a computed/proved ||E||<=q<1. Prove exact coarse elimination identity by block substitution. Scalar commuting diffusion example yields an explicit matrix and its bound; no mesh-independent convergence from the algorithm's name. Multilevel recursive cycle requires separately bounded level operators and recursion, not transfer of two-grid contraction.

pairs.methods_and_promises: **Exact scope.** Nonnegative finite compartments y_i with pair transfers p_ij(y)=d_ji(y)≥0 and `y_i′=Σ_j(p_ij−d_ij)` (external sources/sinks separately specified). First-order Patankar Euler uses transfers frozen at y^n with destination/source weights `y_j^{n+1}/σ_j`, where σ_j>0 is declared and, for first-order consistency, σ_j=y_j^n under a uniform positive lower bound. The resulting matrix has nonpositive off-diagonals, positive diagonal and strict column dominance; prove inverse nonnegativity, positivity and exact summed conservation. Handle initially zero compartments by an explicit zero-consistent transfer-factor representation or a separately analyzed positive denominator regularization; `0/0=0` cannot silently preserve the order proof. The specified second-order positive-interior scheme is MPRK22(1): compute the stage z by Patankar Euler with denominator y^n; then solve `y_i^{n+1}=y_i^n+Δt Σ_j[(p_ij(y^n)+p_ij(z)) y_j^{n+1}/(2z_j)−(d_ij(y^n)+d_ij(z)) y_i^{n+1}/(2z_i)]`. Prove second order on a compact smooth positive tube with uniformly positive stage denominators; conservation/positivity hold independently of that Taylor estimate. Zero-stage and denominator-regularized variants have separate declared contracts, rather than borrowing this order theorem. Do not assert all Patankar variants are second order.
pairs.proof_route: **Proof route / local ownership.** Own finite M-matrix inverse positivity by a nonnegative Neumann series after diagonal scaling, strict dominance/invertibility, conservative column-sum identity, admissible zero-state transfer representation, uniform coefficient bounds, local defect and global order on a compact positive tube. These are not supplied by scalar stiff stability. Derive a residual-to-mass/positivity ledger for inexact solves; positivity after rounded solves is conditional on certified component bounds or a separately analyzed conservative correction. A tiny linear residual alone is not positivity.
pairs.examples: **B examples.** Two-compartment stiff reversible transfer; three-species stoichiometric conservation, with explicit conversion from number to weighted mass variables; extinction/zero-component corner showing denominator failure; explicit Euler negative concentration despite correct first-order truncation. Stipulate kinetics; no empirical reaction law becomes a theorem.

Prove nonnegative update under transport-plus-loss CFL; l1 growth `||n_h^{k+1}||1≤(1+Δt||β||∞)||n_h^k||1`; obtain stability for the difference of two data sets. If compatibility is absent, prove an L1/BV route with reduced regularity rather than reusing the smooth Taylor theorem. State separate age-tail and survival/outflow bounds; finite maximum age is a truncation of an infinite-age model.

A delay equation is not automatically equivalent without a proved renewal/characteristic identity.

A: `finite-basis-projector-energies-and-variational-electronic-structure`.

Let S be a supplied Hermitian positive-definite overlap matrix, 0 < r < n, and transform to an orthonormal basis using an existing Cholesky/spectral factorization. Define the compact set P_r = {P=P*, P²=P, tr P=r}. Input finite h=h*, a self-adjoint real-linear map G on Hermitian matrices, and optional real C² functional E_xc on a neighborhood of P_r. Define E(P)=tr(hP)+1/2 tr(PG(P))+E_xc(P) and its Hermitian Frobenius-gradient F(P)=h+G(P)+grad E_xc(P). The conditional finite-basis HF case is E_xc=0 with a supplied symmetry-compatible Coulomb/exchange tensor; the KS-like case is an explicitly supplied density map and differentiable chosen functional. These are mathematical definitions, not assertions of physical exactness. Prove a global minimizer exists, first variation along P(t)=e^{tK}Pe^{-tK} yields [F(P),P]=0, and a sufficient positive tangent-Hessian condition gives an isolated strict local minimizer modulo orbital gauge. A commutator-zero point need not be a minimum and need not occupy the lowest r eigenvalues. Do not silently equate stationarity and Aufbau SCF.

Also include the finite-temperature density domain 0<=D<=I, tr D=r with continuous endpoint convention 0 log 0=0 and entropy term beta^(-1) tr(D log D+(I-D)log(I-D)). Prove compact-domain minimizer existence; on the interior derive the Fermi–Dirac stationarity equation with chemical potential chosen for the trace, and prove uniqueness of that chemical potential for a fixed finite Hermitian F and 0<r<n. This does not prove uniqueness of a self-consistent density for a nonconvex energy. PC-VAR owns spectral trace derivative and endpoint-continuity suppliers; generic constrained KKT/prox comes from optimization owner.

For nested trial spaces, the finite-basis infimum decreases toward the infimum over their union; equality with a continuum infimum additionally requires density in the energy topology and continuity/liminf hypotheses, each proved for the chosen functional. No general Coulomb HF/DFT existence theorem is smuggled into this statement. Source-model error stays separate.

A residual alone cannot identify the lowest eigenvalue. For a ground state on a compact-resolvent form domain carry the actual form/duality norm and continuum regularity, not the finite-matrix formula verbatim.

**Disposition:** extend-existing numerical guarantee; consume NA15 RK/collocation and NA21 BVP collocation where actually established; this pair concerns IVP high-order quadrature and iterative solution, not duplicate BVP definitions.

On [t,t+h] with distinct nodes c_i in [0,1], let Q_ij=integral_0^ci l_j(s)ds from Lagrange basis. Collocation stage vector satisfies U=1 tensor u+h Q F(U). Explicitly define lower-triangular Q_delta from node-subinterval Euler quadrature; SDC sweep solves U^(k+1)=1 tensor u+h Q_delta F(U^(k+1))+h(Q-Q_delta)F(U^k), component by component with selected implicit branches or explicit preconditioner. If h L||Q_delta||<1, inverse Lipschitz inequality gives contraction factor q=h L||Q-Q_delta||/(1-h L||Q_delta||)<1. Prove stage fixed point equals collocation, geometric iteration residual bound, and finite budget reports nonconvergence. With sufficiently small h and constant predictor, each sweep reduces stage error by O(h); derive the actual order-vs-sweep index rather than promise unlimited order.

Prove local defect O(h^(M+1)) for M nodes from interpolation remainder assuming C^M smooth integrand along the exact flow, and stable propagation gives at least global order M for a step endpoint derived from the same quadrature. Gauss nodes endpoint superconvergence order2M is a separate full proof obligation using orthogonality/defect adjoint or exact RK order conditions; it cannot be inferred from polynomial degree alone. Include one fully proved Gauss-midpoint order2 case even before general superconvergence. Chosen iteration tolerance ||U-U*||<=C h^(p+1) yields collocation order p after accounting for endpoint h F sensitivity; a residual-to-stage inverse bound must convert stopping residual. Spectral node interpolation may have large Lebesgue constants; expose M dependence. No claim of stiff convergence when h L is large; preconditioned scalar linear iteration matrix (I-h lambda Q_delta)^-1 h lambda(Q-Q_delta) is computed and its norm/radius/powers analyzed separately.

pairs.methods_and_promises:
genuinely-new finite Gaussian integral algorithms

A: `gaussian-basis-integral-recurrences-and-boys-error`.

Input finitely many Cartesian Gaussian primitives (polynomial times exp(-a|x-A|²), a>0), real centers and contraction coefficients. Define overlap, kinetic, attraction and two-electron Coulomb integrals as mathematical integrals. Prove absolute convergence including Coulomb singularities; Gaussian product theorem by completing squares; polynomial derivative/raising recurrences by differentiation under an explicit integrable dominating function. Reduce Coulomb integrals using 1/r=(2/sqrt(pi)) integral_0^infinity exp(-t²r²)dt with justified Tonelli and a change of variables to Boys F_m(T)=integral_0^1 t^(2m) exp(-Tt²)dt, m>=0,T>=0. Define finite primitive/contracted integral procedure with a declared recurrence ordering, memoization/work model and error budget. Establish Boys Taylor remainder for small T, positive quadrature enclosure on bounded T, and scaled incomplete-gamma/large-T tail bounds. Prove upward/downward recurrence error amplification and domain-based direction switch. Screening skips a block only with a proved bound (e.g. Coulomb Cauchy–Schwarz), and reports total discarded integral/energy bound rather than claiming exact sparsity.

New suppliers owned PC-GINT: Gaussian moment integrals with parameter derivatives; integral representation and recurrence identities; Boys stable-branch error; positive Coulomb bilinear form/Cauchy–Schwarz; tensor contraction error propagation into PC-VAR energy/gradient, with n/r norms explicit.
